bottom_line: Valsartan vs captopril showed similar all-cause mortality (hazard ratio, 1.00; 97.5 percent confidence interval, 0.90 to 1.11).
implications: These data support that valsartan had similar all-cause mortality to captopril (hazard ratio 1.00; 97.5% CI 0.90 to 1.11) in this post–myocardial infarction high-risk population, while adding valsartan to captopril did not improve survival (hazard ratio 0.98; 97.5% CI 0.89 to 1.09) and increased adverse events. The results do not establish superiority of valsartan over captopril for mortality.

major_points.text: Randomized, double-blind trial in post–myocardial infarction patients with heart failure and/or left ventricular systolic dysfunction, assigning valsartan, captopril, or both.
major_points.quote: We conducted a randomized, double-blind trial at 931 centers in 24 countries.

major_points.text: Patients were randomized 0.5 to 10 days after acute myocardial infarction to valsartan, valsartan plus captopril, or captopril.
major_points.quote: Patients receiving conventional therapy were randomly assigned, 0.5 to 10 days after acute myocardial infarction, to additional therapy with valsartan (4909 patients), valsartan plus captopril (4885 patients), or captopril (4909 patients).

major_points.text: Primary end point was death from any cause.
major_points.quote: The primary end point was death from any cause.

major_points.text: All-cause mortality was similar across groups; valsartan vs captopril HR 1.00 (97.5% CI 0.90 to 1.11).
major_points.quote: The hazard ratio for death in the valsartan group as compared with the captopril group was 1.00 (97.5 percent confidence interval, 0.90 to 1.11; P=0.98)

major_points.text: Combination therapy did not improve survival vs captopril (HR 0.98; 97.5% CI 0.89 to 1.09).
major_points.quote: the hazard ratio for death in the valsartan-and-captopril group as compared with the captopril group was 0.98 (97.5 percent confidence interval, 0.89 to 1.09; P=0.73)

major_points.text: Noninferiority margin for valsartan vs captopril (mortality hazard ratio) was prespecified as 1.13.
major_points.quote: the threshold considered to indicate noninferiority with regard to the hazard ratio for death in the valsartan group as compared with the captopril group was prespecified as 1.13.

major_points.text: The valsartan-and-captopril group had the most drug-related adverse events.
major_points.quote: The valsartan-and-captopril group had the most drug-related adverse events.

major_points.text: With monotherapy, hypotension and renal dysfunction were more common with valsartan; cough, rash, and taste disturbance were more common with captopril.
major_points.quote: With monotherapy, hypotension and renal dysfunction were more common in the valsartan group, and cough, rash, and taste disturbance were more common in the captopril group.
